tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user intent/symptoms (app slow, alarm fired, whether to add IOPS), lists many explicit trigger contexts including cases where the user doesn't name EBS directly ('even if they only say an app or database on EC2 got slower'), explicitly excludes out-of-scope domains, and while long, it remains a focused single-purpose paragraph rather than implementation detail.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a user wants to know why Amazon EBS storage is slow, why an EBS alarm fired, or whether their EBS setup is production-ready, even if they only say an app or database on EC2 got slower or ask whether to add IOPS.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body avoids explaining general concepts (e.g., what EBS is, how CloudWatch works) and jumps straight into domain-specific classification, procedures, and non-obvious rules specific to EBS troubleshooting and review.
tests.evidence: Use this skill to troubleshoot Amazon EBS problems and to review an account's Amazon EBS setup. It has two modes.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (metric thresholds, API lists, error tables) is consistently delegated to references/ files rather than inlined in the body, even within the classification table and workflow steps.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked via markdown link format in the body, confirmed by the References section and inline links throughout Steps 1-4.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is tied to a specific trigger condition (user phrasing, alarm type, or step purpose) rather than being a vague 'see this for details' pointer.
tests.evidence: | "My app is slow", high latency, an alarm on AWS/EBS metrics... | Troubleshoot: performance | [references/troubleshoot-performance.md](references/troubleshoot-performance.md) |

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (modification limits, approval flow, binding layer verdict) are given exact prescriptive language, while flexible areas (e.g., escalation, separate findings) are described with purpose rather than rigid steps, matching specificity to fragility.
tests.evidence: Use current service rules: up to 4 Elastic Volumes modifications per volume per rolling 24 hours.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The classification table designates a clear default path per scenario rather than presenting multiple equal options; no competing tool choices are presented without a default.
tests.evidence: | The user says or the alarm shows | Mode and path | Load |

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable classification-and-procedure approach (classify, load references, run path, validate) applicable to any EBS troubleshooting instance, not a one-off declaration.
tests.evidence: Step 1: Classify the Request ... Step 2: Load the Shared References ... Step 3: Run the Path and Draft the Report

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: A dedicated Gotchas section lists concrete, non-obvious domain facts (unit conversions, metric quirks, stuck-state misconceptions) that correct likely agent mistakes.
tests.evidence: A modification in `optimizing` is not stuck. The new size, IOPS or throughput already applies while it optimizes.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: Output templates/formats are provided (verdict format, review report format) and detailed layouts are appropriately pushed to references/review-report-format.md rather than omitted.
tests.evidence: Review mode uses the rated report in [references/review-report-format.md](references/review-report-format.md).

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The inline 'Troubleshoot verdict format' template is short (6 bullet items), and the larger review report template is correctly stored in references/review-report-format.md rather than inlined.
tests.evidence:

2. **Evidence:** values with units and time window...
